title: Deterministic session-hash ingest shim and schema mapper for Loki migration
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem:
Redwood is ingesting structured logs from many producers (service fleets, SDKs, partner integrations) that use heterogeneous schemas (ECS variants, internal JSON blobs, third-party formats). Downstream migration to Loki exposes two recurring problems: (1) high-cardinality label bloat when unvetted fields are converted to labels, and (2) inability to reliably join logs to traces without leaking raw trace IDs across tenants and external sinks. Multi-line stack traces and inconsistent timestamp encodings further complicate ingestion and indexing.

Goal:
Create an ingestion shim that standardizes incoming logs into a Redwood canonical structured format, computes a deterministic session-hash (privacy-preserving) derived from trace/session identifiers, prunes/normalizes label sets for Loki, and provides backpressure/deduplication and observability for the ingest path. Deliver a safely-rolloutable service with canary and metrics-backed SLOs.

Proposed design summary:
- Input path: Kafka topic "logs-raw" (multi-producer). The shim runs as a horizontally scalable consumer group.
- Transformers: schema-mapper -> multiline combiner -> timestamp normalizer -> session-hasher -> label-pruner -> deduplicator -> output writer.
- Canonical message: RedwoodLogV1 (protobuf) with fields: tenant_id, service, env, level, timestamp_ns, message, json_payload, session_hash, ingest_metadata. We keep trace_id out of labels and store an encrypted compressed kv in the payload for internal debugging only.
- Session-hash algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific salt (retrieved from KMS), input=trace_id||tenant_id||epoch_window, truncated to 16 hex chars. Epoch window rotates daily to limit cross-day linkability. This creates a deterministic but privacy-aware handle to join logs and traces without exposing raw trace IDs.
- Label strategy for Loki: limit to a curated set of labels [tenant, env, svc, level, session_hash]. All other fields go into JSON payload. Enforce label cardinality caps per tenant. High-cardinality fields (user_id, request_id) are hashed and placed in json_payload unless explicitly whitelisted by tenant.
- Backpressure & durability: committed offsets only after successful write to Loki or durable S3 archive. Token-bucket admission with tenant weights; when capacity is exhausted, mark message with backpressure_reason and write to a retry topic "logs-retry".
- Deduplication: 5 minute sliding window keyed on sha1(message||service||ts_bucket) to collapse producer retries. Collision risk estimated <1e-9 for 5M messages/day with sha1; we'll run property tests to validate.
- Observability: Prometheus metrics exposed: logs_ingested_total{tenant,svc}, logs_ingest_errors_total, logs_ingest_latency_seconds histogram, kafka_lag_gauge. Grafana dashboard with P50/P95/P99 ingest latency, error rates, per-tenant cardinality heatmap. Alerting: p99 ingest latency > 0.5s for 5m, error_rate > 1% for 10m, kafka_lag sustained > 30s.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Use protobuf for canonical envelope to reduce encoding ambiguity and size. Keep backwards compatibility with existing JSON pipelines via a compatibility adapter.
- Loki limits: labels are expected to be low-cardinality; avoid adding dynamic fields. The shim enforces label whitelist per tenant and records dropped-label metrics.
- Key management: tenant salt values stored in KMS; access audited. Salt rotation policy: rotate salts per tenant quarterly; on-rotation we recompute hash epoch windows for new traffic and continue to accept older epoch window for 7 days to avoid breakage.
- Privacy: raw trace IDs are encrypted with customer KMS key and stored only in the Kafka "logs-raw-archive" topic and S3 archive for debug only. Downstream Loki payloads only include session_hash.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end ingestion (kafka -> shim -> loki) for a synthetic tenant meets SLO: p50 < 50ms, p99 < 250ms, error rate <0.1% under 5000 rps for 10 minutes.
- Canonical schema is validated via schema tests; at least 95% of historical producers map without manual overrides.
- Label cardinality metrics show no tenant exceeding 10 labels and low-cardinality labels below per-tenant thresholds.
- Canary run 48h stable (no alerts, no >2x baseline errors) before 10% rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) QA environment: unit + integration tests with local Kafka and Loki.
2) Canary: enable feature flag "session-hash-ingest" for a single low-traffic tenant in us-west-2 at 1% traffic. Monitor graphs and alerts for 48h.
3) Incremental expansion to 10% then tenant cohorts (internal services first), then full migration.
4) Post-migration: run a validation job to compare event counts and tail latencies across old/ new pipelines for 7 days.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for schema mapping rules (property-based for field permutations).
- Collision/uniqueness tests for session-hash across large synthetic trace_id sets.
- Load test harness (vegeta-like) to simulate 10k rps and measure ingest latency and broker lag.
- Integration tests that assert Loki ingestion and Grafana queries return expected labels.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Dedup window length vs memory footprint for dedupe index. (Proposed: 5 minutes default, parameterized per tenant.)
- Salt rotation semantics: how long to accept older epochs? (Proposed: 7 days.)
- Should we support optional user-consent to persist original trace IDs for compliance audits?
- Do we expose session_hash as a customer-visible field via Console? Currently we plan internal-only.

Security review notes:
- Access to tenant salts requires KMS decrypt permission; KMS calls are audited.
- PR will include threat model and PII redaction rules for approval.

comments: 2026-03-02 - Marcus Lee: Initial spike complete. Protobuf envelope looks good; multi-line combiner needs improved heuristics for Go vs Java stack frames.

2026-03-04 - Sofia Martinez (reviewer): Suggested label whitelist enforcement at the tenant admission layer to avoid accidental cardinality spikes. Also asked for an explicit metric for labels_dropped_total{tenant}.
2026-03-06 - Marcus Lee: Implemented KMS-backed salt retrieval; created integration stub. Added encrypted trace_id storage to raw archive topic. PR opened: #2873.

2026-03-08 - QA: Integration test failing under 8k rps with kafka_lag growth. Root cause: token-bucket logic rate-limiting causing burst drops. Temporary mitigation: increase consumer parallelism and tune buckets.
Follow-up: add consumer autoscaling policy and circuit-breaker that re-routes to retry topic.
2026-03-11 - Marcus Lee: Fixed dedupe memory leak (use LRU with TTL). Load test at 6k rps stable; ready for 1% canary in us-west-2. Monitoring dashboards prepped.
2026-03-12 - Anya Patel: Security review requested; scheduled for 2026-03-18. Added acceptance criteria and SLOs to ticket.
